## Other projects{style="font-size:0.5em"}

California State Parks - Manzanita Habitat Mapping Using Deep Learning

    The Problem: Arctostaphylos morroensis (Morro manzanita) and Arctostaphylos osoensis (Oso manzanita) are federally threatened and California endemic species restricted to coastal dune and chaparral habitats in San Luis Obispo County. Existing spatial data on its distribution is incomplete or outdated, limiting habitat management, restoration planning, and conservation monitoring. This project will map the distribution of Morro and Oso manzanita within the Los Osos–Morro Bay area using high-resolution drone and satellite imagery. Students will apply supervised classification and deep learning methods to detect and delineate manzanita stands, with field-verified data provided by State Parks for accuracy assessment. Deliverables include polygon layers of mapped habitat, trained deep learning models with documentation, a reproducible workflow, and a methods report. Note: This may be a multi-semester project depending on imagery quality and seasonal conditions.
    Skills: Remote Sensing, Deep Learning, Image Classification, Vegetation Mapping
    Resources:
       + High-resolution drone imagery (available from State Parks)
       + Satellite imagery (e.g. from Sentinel)
       + LiDAR data: https://tukmangeospatial.egnyte.com/dl/pUv4PxwN1E  
       + Aerial imagery of SLO county (and beyond)
       + AVIRIS hyperspectral imagery (aviris.jpl.nasa.gov/dataportal/)
            See also: mdo_aviris_hyperspectral
       + Field-verified training data (provided by agency)
       + Existing species occurrence records (e.g. INaturalist) 
       + Previous group recording: https://calpoly.zoom.us/rec/share/qj2yA5ue6mvH-SzYrpGCNlWmh-mLGW5mlO22wATSpHRcDKDQvr3GwdPwYNI-4x9P.k8rIiPc9UJ42KqI3?startTime=1773680450000

## Other projects{style="font-size:0.5em"}

The Land Conservancy of SLO (LCSLO) - Regional Habitat Suitability & Distribution Modeling for Clarkia speciosa subsp. immaculata and Lupinus ludovicianus
Problem: Existing distribution mapping for Pismo clarkia (Clarkia speciosa subsp. immaculata) and San Luis Obispo lupine (Lupinus ludovicianus) possibly underrepresent population extents. Because significant portions of candidate habitat reside on unsurveyed, privately owned land facing potential commercial and residential development, establishing where these species currently and potentially exist is a critical conservation tool to protect both species. This project builds directly on baseline spatial methodology established in the 2020 Cal Poly study Suitable Habitat for Pismo Clarkia at the Pismo Preserve by scaling the analytical framework from a localized model to a county-wide distribution and habitat suitability assessment across San Luis Obispo County. By integrating historical physical datasets with recently completed fine-scale vegetation mapping, students will refine environmental parameters for both endemic species to create a countywide habitat suitability model. The model will identify current and potential unmapped populations and high-probability occurrence zones across both public and private lands, providing The Land Conservancy of San Luis Obispo County (LCSLO) with an updated, scientifically grounded baseline to target future botanical surveys, inform regional conservation planning, and support future state rare plant listing efforts for San Luis Obispo lupine.
Skills: Reviewing Historic Records, Topographic/Terrain Analysis, Species Distribution Modeling, Vegetation Mapping, Botany, Multi-Criteria/Step Analysis, Literature Review, Field Data Collection, Spatial Statistics
Resources: 

    + Fine Scale Vegetation Mapping (CDFW VegCAMP, CNPS, and Althouse and Meade, Inc.) 
    + Suitable Habitat for Pismo Clarkia at the Pismo Preserve, 2020
    + California Natural Diversity Database (https://wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CNDDB)
    USFWS Senior Biologist/Botanist
    + The Land Conservancy of San Luis Obispo County
    + Sentinel-2 and high-resolution commercial imagery
    + USGS 3DEP / county LiDAR for canopy height models
    + Pacific Veg Map and CAL FIRE FRAP vegetation layers
